+// async_fifo_formal.sv (v3)
+// Formal property set for the Gray-code CDC async FIFO, Phase 1.
+//
+// v1 used concurrent SVA (assert property / $past / $rose / $fell) --
+// unsupported by yosys-slang's current synthesis path.
+// v2 switched to immediate assertions, but relied on `initial assume
+// (!wr_rst_n)` to force a known-good starting state -- also unsupported
+// ("reading net state during design initialization unsupported"), since
+// an `initial` block can only set register values, not sample a live
+// input signal (there's no such thing as "the input's value before
+// time begins" in real hardware).
+//
+// v3 fixes this properly: a STICKY "have we ever actually observed a
+// real reset" flag per domain, set permanently to 1 the first time
+// rst_n is seen low at any clock edge. Checks are only enabled once
+// that flag is set. This is arguably the more correct technique anyway
+// -- it doesn't force reset to happen at exactly time 0, only requires
+// it to have happened at some point in the design's history before we
+// start trusting internal-register consistency, which is the actual
+// real-world guarantee.
+//
+// Properties covered:
+//   1. Gray-code one-bit-change invariant (wr and rd domains)
+//   2. Reset behavior: wr_full low / rd_empty high on the first cycle
+//      after each domain's reset releases
+//   3. wr_full / rd_empty exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+//      using the manually-tracked previous-cycle synchronized pointer
+//   4. Cover: prove full is reachable, prove recovery from full, prove
+//      empty is reached again after data has flowed through
+
+module async_fifo_formal #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+) (
+    // Write domain
+    input logic                  wr_clk,
+    input logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input logic                  wr_en,
+    input logic                  wr_full,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync,
+    // Read domain
+    input logic                  rd_clk,
+    input logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input logic                  rd_en,
+    input logic                  rd_empty,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync
+);
+
+  // ================== Write-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                wr_full_prev;
+  logic                wr_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                wr_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_diff;
+
+  initial wr_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+    // Only trust history once a real reset has actually been observed
+    // at some point -- otherwise the solver is free to start wr_bin
+    // and wr_gray_ptr at two unrelated arbitrary values, which breaks
+    // any comparison for reasons that have nothing to do with the RTL.
+    if (wr_have_reset) begin
+      if (wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (wr_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant -- the property that makes
+          // crossing this pointer through a 2-flop synchronizer safe.
+          // (diff & (diff-1)) == 0 is true iff diff is zero or a single
+          // bit -- the same semantics as $onehot0, without relying on
+          // that system task (unsupported by the current frontend).
+          wr_gray_diff = wr_gray_ptr ^ wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((wr_gray_diff & (wr_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. wr_full must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using rd_gray_sync as it stood one wr_clk cycle ago (that's
+          // the value actually captured into wr_full_next on that edge).
+          assert (wr_full == (
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0])
+          ));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "not full".
+          assert (!wr_full);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: full is reachable, and recovery from full is reachable.
+        cover (wr_full);
+        cover (wr_full_prev && !wr_full);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- async reset can snap pointers to 0
+      // between any two samples, so no invariant is expected to hold
+      // this cycle. Skip checks entirely until reset is released again.
+    end
+
+    wr_gray_ptr_prev  <= wr_gray_ptr;
+    rd_gray_sync_prev <= rd_gray_sync;
+    wr_full_prev      <= wr_full;
+    wr_rst_n_prev     <= wr_rst_n;
+    wr_have_reset     <= wr_have_reset | !wr_rst_n;
+  end
+
+  // ================== Read-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                rd_empty_prev;
+  logic                rd_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                rd_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_diff;
+
+  initial rd_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) begin
+    if (rd_have_reset) begin
+      if (rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (rd_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant, read domain.
+          rd_gray_diff = rd_gray_ptr ^ rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((rd_gray_diff & (rd_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. rd_empty must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using wr_gray_sync as it stood one rd_clk cycle ago.
+          assert (rd_empty == (rd_gray_ptr == wr_gray_sync_prev));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "empty".
+          assert (rd_empty);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: empty is reached again after having been non-empty
+        // (i.e. data flowed through and was fully drained at least once).
+        cover (!rd_empty_prev && rd_empty);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- skip checks entirely, same reasoning
+      // as the write domain above.
+    end
+
+    rd_gray_ptr_prev  <= rd_gray_ptr;
+    wr_gray_sync_prev <= wr_gray_sync;
+    rd_empty_prev     <= rd_empty;
+    rd_rst_n_prev     <= rd_rst_n;
+    rd_have_reset     <= rd_have_reset | !rd_rst_n;
+  end
+
+endmodule
+
+bind async_fifo async_fifo_formal #(
+    .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+) u_formal (.*);

+`timescale 1ns / 1ps
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 1: Dual-Port RAM
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_mem #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4              // Depth = 2**ADDR_WIDTH = 16
+)(
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,    // Gated externally: only HIGH when not full
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data
+);
+
+    // ---- Storage array ----
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] mem [0:(1<<ADDR_WIDTH)-1];
+
+    // Synchronous write
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+        if (wr_en)
+            mem[wr_addr] <= wr_data;
+    end
+
+    // Combinational (async) read
+    assign rd_data = mem[rd_addr];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 2: 2-Flop Synchronizer
+// ==========================================================================
+module sync_2ff #(
+    parameter WIDTH = 1
+)(
+    input  logic             clk,       // Destination clock
+    input  logic             rst_n,     // Destination reset (active-low)
+    input  logic [WIDTH-1:0] d_in,      // Input from source domain
+    output logic [WIDTH-1:0] q_out      // Synchronized output in dest domain
+);
+
+    // Two-stage pipeline
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] meta_ff;  // Stage 1 — may go metastable
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] sync_ff;  // Stage 2 — resolved, safe to use
+
+    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
+        if (!rst_n) begin
+            meta_ff <= '0;
+            sync_ff <= '0;
+        end else begin
+            meta_ff <= d_in;
+            sync_ff <= meta_ff;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign q_out = sync_ff;
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 3: Write Pointer & Full Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    wr_clk,
+    input  logic                    wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    wr_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   wr_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    wr_full
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits (extra MSB for wrap detection)
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_next;
+    logic                wr_full_next;
+
+    // Increment logic
+    assign wr_bin_next  = wr_bin + (wr_en & ~wr_full);
+    assign wr_gray_next = wr_bin_next ^ (wr_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign wr_full_next = (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0]);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk or negedge wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (!wr_rst_n) begin
+            wr_bin <= '0;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            wr_full <= 1'b0;
+        end else begin
+            wr_bin <= wr_bin_next;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= wr_gray_next;
+            wr_full <= wr_full_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign wr_addr = wr_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 4: Read Pointer & Empty Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    rd_clk,
+    input  logic                    rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    rd_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   rd_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    rd_empty
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_next;
+    logic                rd_empty_next;
+
+    assign rd_bin_next = rd_bin + (rd_en & ~rd_empty);
+    assign rd_gray_next = rd_bin_next ^ (rd_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign rd_empty_next = (rd_gray_next == wr_gray_sync);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge rd_clk or negedge rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (!rd_rst_n) begin
+            rd_bin <= '0;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            rd_empty <= 1'b1;
+        end else begin
+            rd_bin <= rd_bin_next;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= rd_gray_next;
+            rd_empty <= rd_empty_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign rd_addr = rd_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+

+// Top-Level Module: Asynchronous FIFO
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo #(

+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_rst_n,

+    input  logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  rd_en,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data,
+    output logic                  rd_empty
+);

+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync;
+

+

+

+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)

+        .rd_gray_ptr(rd_gray_ptr),

+// async_fifo_formal.sv (v3)
+// Formal property set for the Gray-code CDC async FIFO, Phase 1.
+//
+// v1 used concurrent SVA (assert property / $past / $rose / $fell) --
+// unsupported by yosys-slang's current synthesis path.
+// v2 switched to immediate assertions, but relied on `initial assume
+// (!wr_rst_n)` to force a known-good starting state -- also unsupported
+// ("reading net state during design initialization unsupported"), since
+// an `initial` block can only set register values, not sample a live
+// input signal (there's no such thing as "the input's value before
+// time begins" in real hardware).
+//
+// v3 fixes this properly: a STICKY "have we ever actually observed a
+// real reset" flag per domain, set permanently to 1 the first time
+// rst_n is seen low at any clock edge. Checks are only enabled once
+// that flag is set. This is arguably the more correct technique anyway
+// -- it doesn't force reset to happen at exactly time 0, only requires
+// it to have happened at some point in the design's history before we
+// start trusting internal-register consistency, which is the actual
+// real-world guarantee.
+//
+// Properties covered:
+//   1. Gray-code one-bit-change invariant (wr and rd domains)
+//   2. Reset behavior: wr_full low / rd_empty high on the first cycle
+//      after each domain's reset releases
+//   3. wr_full / rd_empty exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+//      using the manually-tracked previous-cycle synchronized pointer
+//   4. Cover: prove full is reachable, prove recovery from full, prove
+//      empty is reached again after data has flowed through
+
+module async_fifo_formal #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+) (
+    // Write domain
+    input logic                  wr_clk,
+    input logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input logic                  wr_en,
+    input logic                  wr_full,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync,
+    // Read domain
+    input logic                  rd_clk,
+    input logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input logic                  rd_en,
+    input logic                  rd_empty,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync
+);
+
+  // ================== Write-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                wr_full_prev;
+  logic                wr_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                wr_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_diff;
+
+  initial wr_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+    // Only trust history once a real reset has actually been observed
+    // at some point -- otherwise the solver is free to start wr_bin
+    // and wr_gray_ptr at two unrelated arbitrary values, which breaks
+    // any comparison for reasons that have nothing to do with the RTL.
+    if (wr_have_reset) begin
+      if (wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (wr_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant -- the property that makes
+          // crossing this pointer through a 2-flop synchronizer safe.
+          // (diff & (diff-1)) == 0 is true iff diff is zero or a single
+          // bit -- the same semantics as $onehot0, without relying on
+          // that system task (unsupported by the current frontend).
+          wr_gray_diff = wr_gray_ptr ^ wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((wr_gray_diff & (wr_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. wr_full must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using rd_gray_sync as it stood one wr_clk cycle ago (that's
+          // the value actually captured into wr_full_next on that edge).
+          assert (wr_full == (
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0])
+          ));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "not full".
+          assert (!wr_full);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: full is reachable, and recovery from full is reachable.
+        cover (wr_full);
+        cover (wr_full_prev && !wr_full);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- async reset can snap pointers to 0
+      // between any two samples, so no invariant is expected to hold
+      // this cycle. Skip checks entirely until reset is released again.
+    end
+
+    wr_gray_ptr_prev  <= wr_gray_ptr;
+    rd_gray_sync_prev <= rd_gray_sync;
+    wr_full_prev      <= wr_full;
+    wr_rst_n_prev     <= wr_rst_n;
+    wr_have_reset     <= wr_have_reset | !wr_rst_n;
+  end
+
+  // ================== Read-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                rd_empty_prev;
+  logic                rd_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                rd_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_diff;
+
+  initial rd_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) begin
+    if (rd_have_reset) begin
+      if (rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (rd_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant, read domain.
+          rd_gray_diff = rd_gray_ptr ^ rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((rd_gray_diff & (rd_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. rd_empty must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using wr_gray_sync as it stood one rd_clk cycle ago.
+          assert (rd_empty == (rd_gray_ptr == wr_gray_sync_prev));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "empty".
+          assert (rd_empty);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: empty is reached again after having been non-empty
+        // (i.e. data flowed through and was fully drained at least once).
+        cover (!rd_empty_prev && rd_empty);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- skip checks entirely, same reasoning
+      // as the write domain above.
+    end
+
+    rd_gray_ptr_prev  <= rd_gray_ptr;
+    wr_gray_sync_prev <= wr_gray_sync;
+    rd_empty_prev     <= rd_empty;
+    rd_rst_n_prev     <= rd_rst_n;
+    rd_have_reset     <= rd_have_reset | !rd_rst_n;
+  end
+
+endmodule
+
+bind async_fifo async_fifo_formal #(
+    .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+) u_formal (.*);

+`timescale 1ns / 1ps

+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 1: Dual-Port RAM
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_mem #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4              // Depth = 2**ADDR_WIDTH = 16
+)(
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,    // Gated externally: only HIGH when not full
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data
+);
+
+    // ---- Storage array ----
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] mem [0:(1<<ADDR_WIDTH)-1];
+
+    // Synchronous write
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+        if (wr_en)
+            mem[wr_addr] <= wr_data;
+    end
+
+    // Combinational (async) read
+    assign rd_data = mem[rd_addr];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 2: 2-Flop Synchronizer
+// ==========================================================================
+module sync_2ff #(
+    parameter WIDTH = 1
+)(
+    input  logic             clk,       // Destination clock
+    input  logic             rst_n,     // Destination reset (active-low)
+    input  logic [WIDTH-1:0] d_in,      // Input from source domain
+    output logic [WIDTH-1:0] q_out      // Synchronized output in dest domain
+);
+
+    // Two-stage pipeline
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] meta_ff;  // Stage 1 — may go metastable
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] sync_ff;  // Stage 2 — resolved, safe to use
+
+    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
+        if (!rst_n) begin
+            meta_ff <= '0;
+            sync_ff <= '0;
+        end else begin
+            meta_ff <= d_in;
+            sync_ff <= meta_ff;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign q_out = sync_ff;
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 3: Write Pointer & Full Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    wr_clk,
+    input  logic                    wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    wr_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   wr_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    wr_full
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits (extra MSB for wrap detection)
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_next;
+    logic                wr_full_next;
+
+    // Increment logic
+    assign wr_bin_next  = wr_bin + (wr_en & ~wr_full);
+    assign wr_gray_next = wr_bin_next ^ (wr_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign wr_full_next = (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0]);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk or negedge wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (!wr_rst_n) begin
+            wr_bin <= '0;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            wr_full <= 1'b0;
+        end else begin
+            wr_bin <= wr_bin_next;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= wr_gray_next;
+            wr_full <= wr_full_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign wr_addr = wr_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 4: Read Pointer & Empty Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    rd_clk,
+    input  logic                    rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    rd_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   rd_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    rd_empty
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_next;
+    logic                rd_empty_next;
+
+    assign rd_bin_next = rd_bin + (rd_en & ~rd_empty);
+    assign rd_gray_next = rd_bin_next ^ (rd_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign rd_empty_next = (rd_gray_next == wr_gray_sync);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge rd_clk or negedge rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (!rd_rst_n) begin
+            rd_bin <= '0;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            rd_empty <= 1'b1;
+        end else begin
+            rd_bin <= rd_bin_next;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= rd_gray_next;
+            rd_empty <= rd_empty_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign rd_addr = rd_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+

+module async_fifo_formal #(

+    input logic                  wr_clk,
+    input logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input logic                  wr_en,
+    input logic                  wr_full,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync,
+    // Read domain
+    input logic                  rd_clk,
+    input logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input logic                  rd_en,
+    input logic                  rd_empty,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync
+);
+
+  // ================== Write-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                wr_full_prev;
+  logic                wr_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                wr_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_diff;

+    // at some point -- otherwise the solver is free to start wr_bin

+          // safe to compare against tracked history.

+          // crossing this pointer through a 2-flop synchronizer safe.
+          // (diff & (diff-1)) == 0 is true iff diff is zero or a single
+          // bit -- the same semantics as $onehot0, without relying on
+          // that system task (unsupported by the current frontend).
+          wr_gray_diff = wr_gray_ptr ^ wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((wr_gray_diff & (wr_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. wr_full must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using rd_gray_sync as it stood one wr_clk cycle ago (that's
+          // the value actually captured into wr_full_next on that edge).
+          assert (wr_full == (
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0])
+          ));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "not full".
+          assert (!wr_full);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: full is reachable, and recovery from full is reachable.
+        cover (wr_full);
+        cover (wr_full_prev && !wr_full);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- async reset can snap pointers to 0
+      // between any two samples, so no invariant is expected to hold
+      // this cycle. Skip checks entirely until reset is released again.
+    end
+
+    wr_gray_ptr_prev  <= wr_gray_ptr;
+    rd_gray_sync_prev <= rd_gray_sync;
+    wr_full_prev      <= wr_full;
+    wr_rst_n_prev     <= wr_rst_n;
+    wr_have_reset     <= wr_have_reset | !wr_rst_n;
+  end
+
+  // ================== Read-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                rd_empty_prev;
+  logic                rd_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                rd_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_diff;
+
+  initial rd_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) begin
+    if (rd_have_reset) begin
+      if (rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (rd_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant, read domain.
+          rd_gray_diff = rd_gray_ptr ^ rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((rd_gray_diff & (rd_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. rd_empty must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using wr_gray_sync as it stood one rd_clk cycle ago.
+          assert (rd_empty == (rd_gray_ptr == wr_gray_sync_prev));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "empty".
+          assert (rd_empty);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: empty is reached again after having been non-empty
+        // (i.e. data flowed through and was fully drained at least once).
+        cover (!rd_empty_prev && rd_empty);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- skip checks entirely, same reasoning
+      // as the write domain above.
+    end
+
+    rd_gray_ptr_prev  <= rd_gray_ptr;
+    wr_gray_sync_prev <= wr_gray_sync;
+    rd_empty_prev     <= rd_empty;
+    rd_rst_n_prev     <= rd_rst_n;
+    rd_have_reset     <= rd_have_reset | !rd_rst_n;
+  end
+
+endmodule
+
+bind async_fifo async_fifo_formal #(
+    .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+) u_formal (.*);

+// async_fifo_integrity_top.sv
+// Phase 2: data-integrity proof for the Gray-code async FIFO.
+//
+// Formal top level. Wraps the unmodified async_fifo, drives it with free
+// inputs, and checks it with a "tagged item" scoreboard.
+//
+// HOW THE CHECK WORKS
+//   The solver picks ONE sequence number (tag_seq) and holds it fixed. The
+//   checker counts accepted writes (wr_cnt) and accepted reads (rd_cnt)
+//   independently of the DUT's own pointers. When write number tag_seq
+//   happens, its data is captured. When read number tag_seq happens, the
+//   data coming out of the FIFO must equal what was captured. Because
+//   tag_seq can be any value, this covers every position in the stream:
+//   a dropped, duplicated, reordered, overwritten or stale item shifts the
+//   numbering and produces a mismatch.
+//
+//   tag_seq has ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits, so it spans two full laps of the memory
+//   (every slot is exercised twice, and every pointer wrap state is hit).
+//   Items beyond 2**(ADDR_WIDTH+1) alias onto the same tag values and are
+//   not individually tracked. State that limit in the paper.
+//
+// ENVIRONMENT ASSUMPTIONS (built structurally, no assume statements)
+//   1. wr_clk and rd_clk are free: any ratio, any phase (needs the
+//      `multiclock on` option in the .sby file).
+//   2. One shared reset, held low until BOTH clocks have ticked at least
+//      once, then released and never asserted again.
+//   3. Reset release timing relative to the clocks is not modeled
+//      (recovery/removal is a physical-design concern).
+//   4. wr_en, wr_data, rd_en are completely free every step.
+//
+// PROPERTIES
+//   P2a  no overflow : an accepted write never happens when the FIFO holds
+//                      DEPTH items
+//   P2b  no underflow: an accepted read never happens when it holds 0 items
+//   P2c  integrity   : the tag_seq-th item read equals the tag_seq-th item
+//                      written (covers ordering, loss, duplication,
+//                      overwrite)
+//   Covers prove the tagged check actually fires, on the second lap too.
+
+module async_fifo_integrity_top #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+) (
+    input logic                  wr_clk,
+    input logic                  rd_clk,
+    input logic                  wr_en,
+    input logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    input logic                  rd_en,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   tag_seq_in   // free; sampled once, then frozen
+);
+
+  localparam SEQ_W = ADDR_WIDTH + 1;
+  localparam int DEPTH = 1 << ADDR_WIDTH;
+
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // Structural reset: low until both clocks have ticked once, then high
+  // forever. Each domain therefore sees at least one edge while in reset.
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  logic wr_seen;
+  logic rd_seen;
+  initial begin
+    wr_seen = 1'b0;
+    rd_seen = 1'b0;
+  end
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) wr_seen <= 1'b1;
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) rd_seen <= 1'b1;
+
+  logic rst_n;
+  assign rst_n = wr_seen & rd_seen;
+
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // Frozen tag index: take a free input at the first write-clock edge,
+  // then never change it. Behaves like an "any constant" without needing
+  // a frontend-specific attribute.
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  logic             tag_set;
+  logic [SEQ_W-1:0] tag_seq;
+  initial tag_set = 1'b0;
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+    if (!tag_set) begin
+      tag_seq <= tag_seq_in;
+      tag_set <= 1'b1;
+    end
+  end
+
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // Device under test (unmodified)
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  logic                  wr_full;
+  logic                  rd_empty;
+  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data;
+
+  async_fifo #(
+      .DATA_WIDTH(DATA_WIDTH),
+      .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+  ) dut (
+      .wr_clk  (wr_clk),
+      .wr_rst_n(rst_n),
+      .wr_en   (wr_en),
+      .wr_data (wr_data),
+      .wr_full (wr_full),
+      .rd_clk  (rd_clk),
+      .rd_rst_n(rst_n),
+      .rd_en   (rd_en),
+      .rd_data (rd_data),
+      .rd_empty(rd_empty)
+  );
+
+  // Accepted operations, as seen at the clock edge (pre-edge flag values)
+  logic wr_acc;
+  logic rd_acc;
+  assign wr_acc = wr_en & ~wr_full;
+  assign rd_acc = rd_en & ~rd_empty;
+
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // Scoreboard state
+  // ------------------------------------------------------------------
+  logic [SEQ_W-1:0]      wr_cnt;        // accepted writes since reset
+  logic [SEQ_W-1:0]      rd_cnt;        // accepted reads since reset
+  logic                  tag_written;
+  logic                  tag_read;
+  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] tag_data;
+
+  // Occupancy, forced to SEQ_W bits so the subtraction wraps correctly
+  logic [SEQ_W-1:0] occ;
+  assign occ = wr_cnt - rd_cnt;
+
+  // ---- Write side ----
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+    if (!rst_n) begin
+      wr_cnt      <= '0;
+      tag_written <= 1'b0;
+      tag_data    <= '0;
+    end else if (wr_acc) begin
+      // P2a: no overflow
+      assert (occ < DEPTH);
+
+      if (!tag_written && wr_cnt == tag_seq) begin
+        tag_written <= 1'b1;
+        tag_data    <= wr_data;
+      end
+      wr_cnt <= wr_cnt + 1'b1;
+    end
+  end
+
+  // ---- Read side ----
+  // rd_data is a combinational read of the slot at the CURRENT read
+  // pointer, so the item being popped at this edge is the pre-edge value.
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) begin
+    if (!rst_n) begin
+      rd_cnt   <= '0;
+      tag_read <= 1'b0;
+    end else begin
+      // Both pointers have wrapped past the first lap
+      cover (wr_cnt[ADDR_WIDTH] && rd_cnt[ADDR_WIDTH]);
+
+      if (rd_acc) begin
+        // P2b: no underflow
+        assert (wr_cnt != rd_cnt);
+
+        if (!tag_read && rd_cnt == tag_seq) begin
+          // P2c: integrity, ordering, no loss, no duplication
+          assert (tag_written);
+          assert (rd_data == tag_data);
+
+          // Non-vacuity: the tagged check really fires
+          cover (tag_written);
+          cover (tag_written && tag_seq[ADDR_WIDTH]);
+          tag_read <= 1'b1;
+        end
+        rd_cnt <= rd_cnt + 1'b1;
+      end
+    end
+  end
+
+endmodule

+`timescale 1ns / 1ps
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 1: Dual-Port RAM
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_mem #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4              // Depth = 2**ADDR_WIDTH = 16
+)(
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,    // Gated externally: only HIGH when not full
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data
+);
+
+    // ---- Storage array ----
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] mem [0:(1<<ADDR_WIDTH)-1];
+
+    // Synchronous write
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+        if (wr_en)
+            mem[wr_addr] <= wr_data;
+    end
+
+    // Combinational (async) read
+    assign rd_data = mem[rd_addr];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 2: 2-Flop Synchronizer
+// ==========================================================================
+module sync_2ff #(
+    parameter WIDTH = 1
+)(
+    input  logic             clk,       // Destination clock
+    input  logic             rst_n,     // Destination reset (active-low)
+    input  logic [WIDTH-1:0] d_in,      // Input from source domain
+    output logic [WIDTH-1:0] q_out      // Synchronized output in dest domain
+);
+
+    // Two-stage pipeline
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] meta_ff;  // Stage 1 — may go metastable
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] sync_ff;  // Stage 2 — resolved, safe to use
+
+    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
+        if (!rst_n) begin
+            meta_ff <= '0;
+            sync_ff <= '0;
+        end else begin
+            meta_ff <= d_in;
+            sync_ff <= meta_ff;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign q_out = sync_ff;
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 3: Write Pointer & Full Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    wr_clk,
+    input  logic                    wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    wr_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   wr_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    wr_full
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits (extra MSB for wrap detection)
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_next;
+    logic                wr_full_next;
+
+    // Increment logic
+    assign wr_bin_next  = wr_bin + (wr_en & ~wr_full);
+    assign wr_gray_next = wr_bin_next ^ (wr_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign wr_full_next = (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0]);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk or negedge wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (!wr_rst_n) begin
+            wr_bin <= '0;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            wr_full <= 1'b0;
+        end else begin
+            wr_bin <= wr_bin_next;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= wr_gray_next;
+            wr_full <= wr_full_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign wr_addr = wr_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 4: Read Pointer & Empty Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    rd_clk,
+    input  logic                    rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    rd_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   rd_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    rd_empty
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_next;
+    logic                rd_empty_next;
+
+    assign rd_bin_next = rd_bin + (rd_en & ~rd_empty);
+    assign rd_gray_next = rd_bin_next ^ (rd_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign rd_empty_next = (rd_gray_next == wr_gray_sync);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge rd_clk or negedge rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (!rd_rst_n) begin
+            rd_bin <= '0;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            rd_empty <= 1'b1;
+        end else begin
+            rd_bin <= rd_bin_next;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= rd_gray_next;
+            rd_empty <= rd_empty_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign rd_addr = rd_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Top-Level Module: Asynchronous FIFO
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    // Write domain
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    output logic                  wr_full,
+    // Read domain
+    input  logic                  rd_clk,
+    input  logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  rd_en,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data,
+    output logic                  rd_empty
+);
+
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync;
+
+    logic wr_en_gated;
+
+    assign wr_en_gated = wr_en & ~wr_full;
+
+    // RAM
+    async_fifo_mem #(
+        .DATA_WIDTH(DATA_WIDTH),
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_mem (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_en(wr_en_gated),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_data(wr_data),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_data(rd_data)
+    );
+
+    // Write pointer & full logic
+    async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_wr_ptr (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .wr_en(wr_en),
+        .rd_gray_sync(rd_gray_sync),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_gray_ptr(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .wr_full(wr_full)
+    );
+
+    // Read pointer & empty logic
+    async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_rd_ptr (
+        .rd_clk(rd_clk),
+        .rd_rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .rd_en(rd_en),
+        .wr_gray_sync(wr_gray_sync),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_gray_ptr(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .rd_empty(rd_empty)
+    );
+
+    // Synchronizers
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_wr2rd (
+        .clk(rd_clk),
+        .rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .d_in(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(wr_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_rd2wr (
+        .clk(wr_clk),
+        .rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .d_in(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(rd_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+endmodule

+// async_fifo_formal.sv (v3)
+// Formal property set for the Gray-code CDC async FIFO, Phase 1.
+//
+// v1 used concurrent SVA (assert property / $past / $rose / $fell) --
+// unsupported by yosys-slang's current synthesis path.
+// v2 switched to immediate assertions, but relied on `initial assume
+// (!wr_rst_n)` to force a known-good starting state -- also unsupported
+// ("reading net state during design initialization unsupported"), since
+// an `initial` block can only set register values, not sample a live
+// input signal (there's no such thing as "the input's value before
+// time begins" in real hardware).
+//
+// v3 fixes this properly: a STICKY "have we ever actually observed a
+// real reset" flag per domain, set permanently to 1 the first time
+// rst_n is seen low at any clock edge. Checks are only enabled once
+// that flag is set. This is arguably the more correct technique anyway
+// -- it doesn't force reset to happen at exactly time 0, only requires
+// it to have happened at some point in the design's history before we
+// start trusting internal-register consistency, which is the actual
+// real-world guarantee.
+//
+// Properties covered:
+//   1. Gray-code one-bit-change invariant (wr and rd domains)
+//   2. Reset behavior: wr_full low / rd_empty high on the first cycle
+//      after each domain's reset releases
+//   3. wr_full / rd_empty exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+//      using the manually-tracked previous-cycle synchronized pointer
+//   4. Cover: prove full is reachable, prove recovery from full, prove
+//      empty is reached again after data has flowed through
+
+module async_fifo_formal #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+) (
+    // Write domain
+    input logic                  wr_clk,
+    input logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input logic                  wr_en,
+    input logic                  wr_full,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync,
+    // Read domain
+    input logic                  rd_clk,
+    input logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input logic                  rd_en,
+    input logic                  rd_empty,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync
+);
+
+  // ================== Write-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                wr_full_prev;
+  logic                wr_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                wr_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_diff;
+
+  initial wr_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+    // Only trust history once a real reset has actually been observed
+    // at some point -- otherwise the solver is free to start wr_bin
+    // and wr_gray_ptr at two unrelated arbitrary values, which breaks
+    // any comparison for reasons that have nothing to do with the RTL.
+    if (wr_have_reset) begin
+      if (wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (wr_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant -- the property that makes
+          // crossing this pointer through a 2-flop synchronizer safe.
+          // (diff & (diff-1)) == 0 is true iff diff is zero or a single
+          // bit -- the same semantics as $onehot0, without relying on
+          // that system task (unsupported by the current frontend).
+          wr_gray_diff = wr_gray_ptr ^ wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((wr_gray_diff & (wr_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. wr_full must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using rd_gray_sync as it stood one wr_clk cycle ago (that's
+          // the value actually captured into wr_full_next on that edge).
+          assert (wr_full == (
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0])
+          ));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "not full".
+          assert (!wr_full);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: full is reachable, and recovery from full is reachable.
+        cover (wr_full);
+        cover (wr_full_prev && !wr_full);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- async reset can snap pointers to 0
+      // between any two samples, so no invariant is expected to hold
+      // this cycle. Skip checks entirely until reset is released again.
+    end
+
+    wr_gray_ptr_prev  <= wr_gray_ptr;
+    rd_gray_sync_prev <= rd_gray_sync;
+    wr_full_prev      <= wr_full;
+    wr_rst_n_prev     <= wr_rst_n;
+    wr_have_reset     <= wr_have_reset | !wr_rst_n;
+  end
+
+  // ================== Read-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                rd_empty_prev;
+  logic                rd_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                rd_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_diff;
+
+  initial rd_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) begin
+    if (rd_have_reset) begin
+      if (rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (rd_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant, read domain.
+          rd_gray_diff = rd_gray_ptr ^ rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((rd_gray_diff & (rd_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. rd_empty must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using wr_gray_sync as it stood one rd_clk cycle ago.
+          assert (rd_empty == (rd_gray_ptr == wr_gray_sync_prev));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "empty".
+          assert (rd_empty);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: empty is reached again after having been non-empty
+        // (i.e. data flowed through and was fully drained at least once).
+        cover (!rd_empty_prev && rd_empty);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- skip checks entirely, same reasoning
+      // as the write domain above.
+    end
+
+    rd_gray_ptr_prev  <= rd_gray_ptr;
+    wr_gray_sync_prev <= wr_gray_sync;
+    rd_empty_prev     <= rd_empty;
+    rd_rst_n_prev     <= rd_rst_n;
+    rd_have_reset     <= rd_have_reset | !rd_rst_n;
+  end
+
+endmodule
+
+bind async_fifo async_fifo_formal #(
+    .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+) u_formal (.*);

+`timescale 1ns / 1ps
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 1: Dual-Port RAM
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_mem #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4              // Depth = 2**ADDR_WIDTH = 16
+)(
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,    // Gated externally: only HIGH when not full
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data
+);
+
+    // ---- Storage array ----
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] mem [0:(1<<ADDR_WIDTH)-1];
+
+    // Synchronous write
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+        if (wr_en)
+            mem[wr_addr] <= wr_data;
+    end
+
+    // Combinational (async) read
+    assign rd_data = mem[rd_addr];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 2: 2-Flop Synchronizer
+// ==========================================================================
+module sync_2ff #(
+    parameter WIDTH = 1
+)(
+    input  logic             clk,       // Destination clock
+    input  logic             rst_n,     // Destination reset (active-low)
+    input  logic [WIDTH-1:0] d_in,      // Input from source domain
+    output logic [WIDTH-1:0] q_out      // Synchronized output in dest domain
+);
+
+    // Two-stage pipeline
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] meta_ff;  // Stage 1 — may go metastable
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] sync_ff;  // Stage 2 — resolved, safe to use
+
+    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
+        if (!rst_n) begin
+            meta_ff <= '0;
+            sync_ff <= '0;
+        end else begin
+            meta_ff <= d_in;
+            sync_ff <= meta_ff;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign q_out = sync_ff;
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 3: Write Pointer & Full Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    wr_clk,
+    input  logic                    wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    wr_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   wr_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    wr_full
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits (extra MSB for wrap detection)
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_next;
+    logic                wr_full_next;
+
+    // Increment logic
+    assign wr_bin_next  = wr_bin + (wr_en & ~wr_full);
+    assign wr_gray_next = wr_bin_next ^ (wr_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign wr_full_next = (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0]);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk or negedge wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (!wr_rst_n) begin
+            wr_bin <= '0;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            wr_full <= 1'b0;
+        end else begin
+            wr_bin <= wr_bin_next;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= wr_gray_next;
+            wr_full <= wr_full_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign wr_addr = wr_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 4: Read Pointer & Empty Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    rd_clk,
+    input  logic                    rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    rd_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   rd_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    rd_empty
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_next;
+    logic                rd_empty_next;
+
+    assign rd_bin_next = rd_bin + (rd_en & ~rd_empty);
+    assign rd_gray_next = rd_bin_next ^ (rd_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign rd_empty_next = (rd_gray_next == wr_gray_sync);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge rd_clk or negedge rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (!rd_rst_n) begin
+            rd_bin <= '0;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            rd_empty <= 1'b1;
+        end else begin
+            rd_bin <= rd_bin_next;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= rd_gray_next;
+            rd_empty <= rd_empty_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign rd_addr = rd_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Top-Level Module: Asynchronous FIFO
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    // Write domain
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    output logic                  wr_full,
+    // Read domain
+    input  logic                  rd_clk,
+    input  logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  rd_en,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data,
+    output logic                  rd_empty
+);
+
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync;
+
+    logic wr_en_gated;
+
+    assign wr_en_gated = wr_en & ~wr_full;
+
+    // RAM
+    async_fifo_mem #(
+        .DATA_WIDTH(DATA_WIDTH),
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_mem (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_en(wr_en_gated),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_data(wr_data),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_data(rd_data)
+    );
+
+    // Write pointer & full logic
+    async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_wr_ptr (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .wr_en(wr_en),
+        .rd_gray_sync(rd_gray_sync),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_gray_ptr(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .wr_full(wr_full)
+    );
+
+    // Read pointer & empty logic
+    async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_rd_ptr (
+        .rd_clk(rd_clk),
+        .rd_rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .rd_en(rd_en),
+        .wr_gray_sync(wr_gray_sync),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_gray_ptr(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .rd_empty(rd_empty)
+    );
+
+    // Synchronizers
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_wr2rd (
+        .clk(rd_clk),
+        .rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .d_in(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(wr_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_rd2wr (
+        .clk(wr_clk),
+        .rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .d_in(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(rd_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+endmodule

+// async_fifo_formal.sv (v3)
+// Formal property set for the Gray-code CDC async FIFO, Phase 1.
+//
+// v1 used concurrent SVA (assert property / $past / $rose / $fell) --
+// unsupported by yosys-slang's current synthesis path.
+// v2 switched to immediate assertions, but relied on `initial assume
+// (!wr_rst_n)` to force a known-good starting state -- also unsupported
+// ("reading net state during design initialization unsupported"), since
+// an `initial` block can only set register values, not sample a live
+// input signal (there's no such thing as "the input's value before
+// time begins" in real hardware).
+//
+// v3 fixes this properly: a STICKY "have we ever actually observed a
+// real reset" flag per domain, set permanently to 1 the first time
+// rst_n is seen low at any clock edge. Checks are only enabled once
+// that flag is set. This is arguably the more correct technique anyway
+// -- it doesn't force reset to happen at exactly time 0, only requires
+// it to have happened at some point in the design's history before we
+// start trusting internal-register consistency, which is the actual
+// real-world guarantee.
+//
+// Properties covered:
+//   1. Gray-code one-bit-change invariant (wr and rd domains)
+//   2. Reset behavior: wr_full low / rd_empty high on the first cycle
+//      after each domain's reset releases
+//   3. wr_full / rd_empty exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+//      using the manually-tracked previous-cycle synchronized pointer
+//   4. Cover: prove full is reachable, prove recovery from full, prove
+//      empty is reached again after data has flowed through
+
+module async_fifo_formal #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+) (
+    // Write domain
+    input logic                  wr_clk,
+    input logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input logic                  wr_en,
+    input logic                  wr_full,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync,
+    // Read domain
+    input logic                  rd_clk,
+    input logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input logic                  rd_en,
+    input logic                  rd_empty,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync
+);
+
+  // ================== Write-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                wr_full_prev;
+  logic                wr_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                wr_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_diff;
+
+  initial wr_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+    // Only trust history once a real reset has actually been observed
+    // at some point -- otherwise the solver is free to start wr_bin
+    // and wr_gray_ptr at two unrelated arbitrary values, which breaks
+    // any comparison for reasons that have nothing to do with the RTL.
+    if (wr_have_reset) begin
+      if (wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (wr_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant -- the property that makes
+          // crossing this pointer through a 2-flop synchronizer safe.
+          // (diff & (diff-1)) == 0 is true iff diff is zero or a single
+          // bit -- the same semantics as $onehot0, without relying on
+          // that system task (unsupported by the current frontend).
+          wr_gray_diff = wr_gray_ptr ^ wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((wr_gray_diff & (wr_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. wr_full must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using rd_gray_sync as it stood one wr_clk cycle ago (that's
+          // the value actually captured into wr_full_next on that edge).
+          assert (wr_full == (
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0])
+          ));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "not full".
+          assert (!wr_full);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: full is reachable, and recovery from full is reachable.
+        cover (wr_full);
+        cover (wr_full_prev && !wr_full);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- async reset can snap pointers to 0
+      // between any two samples, so no invariant is expected to hold
+      // this cycle. Skip checks entirely until reset is released again.
+    end
+
+    wr_gray_ptr_prev  <= wr_gray_ptr;
+    rd_gray_sync_prev <= rd_gray_sync;
+    wr_full_prev      <= wr_full;
+    wr_rst_n_prev     <= wr_rst_n;
+    wr_have_reset     <= wr_have_reset | !wr_rst_n;
+  end
+
+  // ================== Read-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                rd_empty_prev;
+  logic                rd_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                rd_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_diff;
+
+  initial rd_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) begin
+    if (rd_have_reset) begin
+      if (rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (rd_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant, read domain.
+          rd_gray_diff = rd_gray_ptr ^ rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((rd_gray_diff & (rd_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. rd_empty must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using wr_gray_sync as it stood one rd_clk cycle ago.
+          assert (rd_empty == (rd_gray_ptr == wr_gray_sync_prev));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "empty".
+          assert (rd_empty);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: empty is reached again after having been non-empty
+        // (i.e. data flowed through and was fully drained at least once).
+        cover (!rd_empty_prev && rd_empty);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- skip checks entirely, same reasoning
+      // as the write domain above.
+    end
+
+    rd_gray_ptr_prev  <= rd_gray_ptr;
+    wr_gray_sync_prev <= wr_gray_sync;
+    rd_empty_prev     <= rd_empty;
+    rd_rst_n_prev     <= rd_rst_n;
+    rd_have_reset     <= rd_have_reset | !rd_rst_n;
+  end
+
+endmodule
+
+bind async_fifo async_fifo_formal #(
+    .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+) u_formal (.*);

+`timescale 1ns / 1ps
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 1: Dual-Port RAM
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_mem #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4              // Depth = 2**ADDR_WIDTH = 16
+)(
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,    // Gated externally: only HIGH when not full
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data
+);
+
+    // ---- Storage array ----
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] mem [0:(1<<ADDR_WIDTH)-1];
+
+    // Synchronous write
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+        if (wr_en)
+            mem[wr_addr] <= wr_data;
+    end
+
+    // Combinational (async) read
+    assign rd_data = mem[rd_addr];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 2: 2-Flop Synchronizer
+// ==========================================================================
+module sync_2ff #(
+    parameter WIDTH = 1
+)(
+    input  logic             clk,       // Destination clock
+    input  logic             rst_n,     // Destination reset (active-low)
+    input  logic [WIDTH-1:0] d_in,      // Input from source domain
+    output logic [WIDTH-1:0] q_out      // Synchronized output in dest domain
+);
+
+    // Two-stage pipeline
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] meta_ff;  // Stage 1 — may go metastable
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] sync_ff;  // Stage 2 — resolved, safe to use
+
+    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
+        if (!rst_n) begin
+            meta_ff <= '0;
+            sync_ff <= '0;
+        end else begin
+            meta_ff <= d_in;
+            sync_ff <= meta_ff;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign q_out = sync_ff;
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 3: Write Pointer & Full Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    wr_clk,
+    input  logic                    wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    wr_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   wr_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    wr_full
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits (extra MSB for wrap detection)
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_next;
+    logic                wr_full_next;
+
+    // Increment logic
+    assign wr_bin_next  = wr_bin + (wr_en & ~wr_full);
+    assign wr_gray_next = wr_bin_next ^ (wr_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign wr_full_next = (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0]);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk or negedge wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (!wr_rst_n) begin
+            wr_bin <= '0;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            wr_full <= 1'b0;
+        end else begin
+            wr_bin <= wr_bin_next;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= wr_gray_next;
+            wr_full <= wr_full_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign wr_addr = wr_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 4: Read Pointer & Empty Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    rd_clk,
+    input  logic                    rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    rd_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   rd_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    rd_empty
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_next;
+    logic                rd_empty_next;
+
+    assign rd_bin_next = rd_bin + (rd_en & ~rd_empty);
+    assign rd_gray_next = rd_bin_next ^ (rd_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign rd_empty_next = (rd_gray_next == wr_gray_sync);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge rd_clk or negedge rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (!rd_rst_n) begin
+            rd_bin <= '0;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            rd_empty <= 1'b1;
+        end else begin
+            rd_bin <= rd_bin_next;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= rd_gray_next;
+            rd_empty <= rd_empty_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign rd_addr = rd_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Top-Level Module: Asynchronous FIFO
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    // Write domain
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    output logic                  wr_full,
+    // Read domain
+    input  logic                  rd_clk,
+    input  logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  rd_en,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data,
+    output logic                  rd_empty
+);
+
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync;
+
+    logic wr_en_gated;
+
+    assign wr_en_gated = wr_en & ~wr_full;
+
+    // RAM
+    async_fifo_mem #(
+        .DATA_WIDTH(DATA_WIDTH),
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_mem (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_en(wr_en_gated),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_data(wr_data),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_data(rd_data)
+    );
+
+    // Write pointer & full logic
+    async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_wr_ptr (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .wr_en(wr_en),
+        .rd_gray_sync(rd_gray_sync),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_gray_ptr(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .wr_full(wr_full)
+    );
+
+    // Read pointer & empty logic
+    async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_rd_ptr (
+        .rd_clk(rd_clk),
+        .rd_rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .rd_en(rd_en),
+        .wr_gray_sync(wr_gray_sync),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_gray_ptr(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .rd_empty(rd_empty)
+    );
+
+    // Synchronizers
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_wr2rd (
+        .clk(rd_clk),
+        .rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .d_in(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(wr_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_rd2wr (
+        .clk(wr_clk),
+        .rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .d_in(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(rd_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+endmodule

+// async_fifo_formal.sv (v3)
+// Formal property set for the Gray-code CDC async FIFO, Phase 1.
+//
+// v1 used concurrent SVA (assert property / $past / $rose / $fell) --
+// unsupported by yosys-slang's current synthesis path.
+// v2 switched to immediate assertions, but relied on `initial assume
+// (!wr_rst_n)` to force a known-good starting state -- also unsupported
+// ("reading net state during design initialization unsupported"), since
+// an `initial` block can only set register values, not sample a live
+// input signal (there's no such thing as "the input's value before
+// time begins" in real hardware).
+//
+// v3 fixes this properly: a STICKY "have we ever actually observed a
+// real reset" flag per domain, set permanently to 1 the first time
+// rst_n is seen low at any clock edge. Checks are only enabled once
+// that flag is set. This is arguably the more correct technique anyway
+// -- it doesn't force reset to happen at exactly time 0, only requires
+// it to have happened at some point in the design's history before we
+// start trusting internal-register consistency, which is the actual
+// real-world guarantee.
+//
+// Properties covered:
+//   1. Gray-code one-bit-change invariant (wr and rd domains)
+//   2. Reset behavior: wr_full low / rd_empty high on the first cycle
+//      after each domain's reset releases
+//   3. wr_full / rd_empty exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+//      using the manually-tracked previous-cycle synchronized pointer
+//   4. Cover: prove full is reachable, prove recovery from full, prove
+//      empty is reached again after data has flowed through
+
+module async_fifo_formal #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+) (
+    // Write domain
+    input logic                  wr_clk,
+    input logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input logic                  wr_en,
+    input logic                  wr_full,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync,
+    // Read domain
+    input logic                  rd_clk,
+    input logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input logic                  rd_en,
+    input logic                  rd_empty,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync
+);
+
+  // ================== Write-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                wr_full_prev;
+  logic                wr_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                wr_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_diff;
+
+  initial wr_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+    // Only trust history once a real reset has actually been observed
+    // at some point -- otherwise the solver is free to start wr_bin
+    // and wr_gray_ptr at two unrelated arbitrary values, which breaks
+    // any comparison for reasons that have nothing to do with the RTL.
+    if (wr_have_reset) begin
+      if (wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (wr_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant -- the property that makes
+          // crossing this pointer through a 2-flop synchronizer safe.
+          // (diff & (diff-1)) == 0 is true iff diff is zero or a single
+          // bit -- the same semantics as $onehot0, without relying on
+          // that system task (unsupported by the current frontend).
+          wr_gray_diff = wr_gray_ptr ^ wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((wr_gray_diff & (wr_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. wr_full must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using rd_gray_sync as it stood one wr_clk cycle ago (that's
+          // the value actually captured into wr_full_next on that edge).
+          assert (wr_full == (
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0])
+          ));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "not full".
+          assert (!wr_full);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: full is reachable, and recovery from full is reachable.
+        cover (wr_full);
+        cover (wr_full_prev && !wr_full);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- async reset can snap pointers to 0
+      // between any two samples, so no invariant is expected to hold
+      // this cycle. Skip checks entirely until reset is released again.
+    end
+
+    wr_gray_ptr_prev  <= wr_gray_ptr;
+    rd_gray_sync_prev <= rd_gray_sync;
+    wr_full_prev      <= wr_full;
+    wr_rst_n_prev     <= wr_rst_n;
+    wr_have_reset     <= wr_have_reset | !wr_rst_n;
+  end
+
+  // ================== Read-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                rd_empty_prev;
+  logic                rd_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                rd_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_diff;
+
+  initial rd_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) begin
+    if (rd_have_reset) begin
+      if (rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (rd_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant, read domain.
+          rd_gray_diff = rd_gray_ptr ^ rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((rd_gray_diff & (rd_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. rd_empty must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using wr_gray_sync as it stood one rd_clk cycle ago.
+          assert (rd_empty == (rd_gray_ptr == wr_gray_sync_prev));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "empty".
+          assert (rd_empty);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: empty is reached again after having been non-empty
+        // (i.e. data flowed through and was fully drained at least once).
+        cover (!rd_empty_prev && rd_empty);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- skip checks entirely, same reasoning
+      // as the write domain above.
+    end
+
+    rd_gray_ptr_prev  <= rd_gray_ptr;
+    wr_gray_sync_prev <= wr_gray_sync;
+    rd_empty_prev     <= rd_empty;
+    rd_rst_n_prev     <= rd_rst_n;
+    rd_have_reset     <= rd_have_reset | !rd_rst_n;
+  end
+
+endmodule
+
+bind async_fifo async_fifo_formal #(
+    .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+) u_formal (.*);
