+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Plot proof runtime vs FIFO depth from sweep_results.csv.
+
+Usage: python3 plot_sweep.py [sweep_results.csv] [out.png]
+Needs matplotlib; if it is missing, a markdown table is printed instead.
+Runs that did not PASS are drawn as red crosses so a timeout or failure
+is never mistaken for a fast proof.
+"""
+import csv
+import sys
+from collections import defaultdict
+
+src = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "sweep_results.csv"
+dst = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "runtime_vs_depth.png"
+
+rows = []
+with open(src, newline="") as f:
+    lines = [ln for ln in f if not ln.startswith("#")]
+for r in csv.DictReader(lines):
+    r["entries"] = int(r["entries"])
+    r["seconds"] = float(r["seconds"])
+    rows.append(r)
+

+

+    import matplotlib
+    matplotlib.use("Agg")

+    print("\nmatplotlib not installed; skipping the figure.")

+

+for r in rows:
+    series[(r["sby_file"], r["task"])].append(r)
+

+for (sby, task), pts in sorted(series.items()):
+    pts.sort(key=lambda r: r["entries"])
+    name = f"{sby.replace('.sby', '')}: {task}"
+    ok = [p for p in pts if p["status"] == "PASS"]
+    ax.plot([p["entries"] for p in ok], [max(p["seconds"], 0.5) for p in ok],
+            marker="o", label=name)
+    bad = [p for p in pts if p["status"] != "PASS"]
+    if bad:

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Phase 3 parameter sweep.
+# Re-runs the proof sets at several FIFO depths and records status + wall time.
+#
+# Run from the folder holding async_fifo.sv, async_fifo_formal.sv,
+# async_fifo_integrity_top.sv and the .sby files:
+#     chmod +x sweep.sh && ./sweep.sh
+#
+# Overrides (all optional), e.g.:
+#     ADDRS="2 3" TIMEOUT=600 ./sweep.sh
+#     TASKS="bmc cover" ./sweep.sh
+#     DATA_W=4 ./sweep.sh        # narrower data path = faster (FIFO is data-independent)
+
+set -u
+
+ADDRS=${ADDRS:-"2 3 4 5"}                     # ADDR_WIDTH values; depth = 2**ADDR_WIDTH
+DATA_W=${DATA_W:-8}
+TIMEOUT=${TIMEOUT:-1800}                      # seconds per run
+TASKS=${TASKS:-"bmc prove cover"}
+SBY_FILES=${SBY_FILES:-"async_fifo_multiclock.sby async_fifo_integrity.sby"}
+SV_FILES=${SV_FILES:-"async_fifo.sv async_fifo_formal.sv async_fifo_integrity_top.sv"}
+WORK=sweep_work
+OUT=sweep_results.csv
+
+mkdir -p "$WORK"
+
+{
+  echo "# date: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
+  echo "# yosys: $(yosys -V 2>&1 | head -1)"
+  echo "# z3: $(z3 --version 2>&1 | head -1)"
+  echo "# data_width: $DATA_W  timeout_s: $TIMEOUT"
+  echo "addr_width,entries,bmc_depth,sby_file,task,status,seconds"
+} > "$OUT"
+
+for N in $ADDRS; do
+  ENTRIES=$((1 << N))
+  # Deep enough to push the highest tag index (2**(N+1)-1) through write,
+  # 2-flop sync and read.
+  D=$(( (1 << (N + 1)) + 12 ))
+  WD="$WORK/addr_$N"
+  rm -rf "$WD"
+  mkdir -p "$WD"
+
+  for f in $SV_FILES $SBY_FILES; do
+    if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
+      echo "missing file: $f (run from the project folder)" >&2
+      exit 1
+    fi
+    cp "$f" "$WD/"
+  done
+
+  # Rewrite parameter defaults in the copies only; originals stay untouched.
+  sed -i -E "s/(parameter[[:space:]]+ADDR_WIDTH[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*)[0-9]+/\1${N}/" "$WD"/*.sv
+  sed -i -E "s/(parameter[[:space:]]+DATA_WIDTH[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*)[0-9]+/\1${DATA_W}/" "$WD"/*.sv
+  sed -i -E "s/(depth )[0-9]+/\1${D}/" "$WD"/*.sby
+
+  for SBY in $SBY_FILES; do
+    for T in $TASKS; do
+      echo ">>> ADDR_WIDTH=$N ($ENTRIES entries)  depth=$D  $SBY  $T"
+      START=$(date +%s)
+      ( cd "$WD" && timeout "$TIMEOUT" sby -f "$SBY" "$T" > "log_${SBY%.sby}_${T}.txt" 2>&1 )
+      RC=$?
+      END=$(date +%s)
+      case $RC in
+        0)   STATUS=PASS ;;
+        2)   STATUS=FAIL ;;
+        4)   STATUS=UNKNOWN ;;
+        8)   STATUS=TIMEOUT ;;
+        16)  STATUS=ERROR ;;
+        124) STATUS=TIMEOUT ;;
+        *)   STATUS="RC$RC" ;;
+      esac
+      echo "$N,$ENTRIES,$D,$SBY,$T,$STATUS,$((END - START))" >> "$OUT"
+      echo "    -> $STATUS in $((END - START))s"
+    done
+  done
+done
+
+echo
+echo "Results written to $OUT"
+grep -v '^#' "$OUT" | column -s, -t

+// async_fifo_formal.sv (v3)
+// Formal property set for the Gray-code CDC async FIFO, Phase 1.
+//
+// v1 used concurrent SVA (assert property / $past / $rose / $fell) --
+// unsupported by yosys-slang's current synthesis path.
+// v2 switched to immediate assertions, but relied on `initial assume
+// (!wr_rst_n)` to force a known-good starting state -- also unsupported
+// ("reading net state during design initialization unsupported"), since
+// an `initial` block can only set register values, not sample a live
+// input signal (there's no such thing as "the input's value before
+// time begins" in real hardware).
+//
+// v3 fixes this properly: a STICKY "have we ever actually observed a
+// real reset" flag per domain, set permanently to 1 the first time
+// rst_n is seen low at any clock edge. Checks are only enabled once
+// that flag is set. This is arguably the more correct technique anyway
+// -- it doesn't force reset to happen at exactly time 0, only requires
+// it to have happened at some point in the design's history before we
+// start trusting internal-register consistency, which is the actual
+// real-world guarantee.
+//
+// Properties covered:
+//   1. Gray-code one-bit-change invariant (wr and rd domains)
+//   2. Reset behavior: wr_full low / rd_empty high on the first cycle
+//      after each domain's reset releases
+//   3. wr_full / rd_empty exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+//      using the manually-tracked previous-cycle synchronized pointer
+//   4. Cover: prove full is reachable, prove recovery from full, prove
+//      empty is reached again after data has flowed through
+
+module async_fifo_formal #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+) (
+    // Write domain
+    input logic                  wr_clk,
+    input logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input logic                  wr_en,
+    input logic                  wr_full,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync,
+    // Read domain
+    input logic                  rd_clk,
+    input logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input logic                  rd_en,
+    input logic                  rd_empty,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync
+);
+
+  // ================== Write-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                wr_full_prev;
+  logic                wr_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                wr_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_diff;
+
+  initial wr_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+    // Only trust history once a real reset has actually been observed
+    // at some point -- otherwise the solver is free to start wr_bin
+    // and wr_gray_ptr at two unrelated arbitrary values, which breaks
+    // any comparison for reasons that have nothing to do with the RTL.
+    if (wr_have_reset) begin
+      if (wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (wr_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant -- the property that makes
+          // crossing this pointer through a 2-flop synchronizer safe.
+          // (diff & (diff-1)) == 0 is true iff diff is zero or a single
+          // bit -- the same semantics as $onehot0, without relying on
+          // that system task (unsupported by the current frontend).
+          wr_gray_diff = wr_gray_ptr ^ wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((wr_gray_diff & (wr_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. wr_full must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using rd_gray_sync as it stood one wr_clk cycle ago (that's
+          // the value actually captured into wr_full_next on that edge).
+          assert (wr_full == (
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0])
+          ));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "not full".
+          assert (!wr_full);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: full is reachable, and recovery from full is reachable.
+        cover (wr_full);
+        cover (wr_full_prev && !wr_full);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- async reset can snap pointers to 0
+      // between any two samples, so no invariant is expected to hold
+      // this cycle. Skip checks entirely until reset is released again.
+    end
+
+    wr_gray_ptr_prev  <= wr_gray_ptr;
+    rd_gray_sync_prev <= rd_gray_sync;
+    wr_full_prev      <= wr_full;
+    wr_rst_n_prev     <= wr_rst_n;
+    wr_have_reset     <= wr_have_reset | !wr_rst_n;
+  end
+
+  // ================== Read-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                rd_empty_prev;
+  logic                rd_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                rd_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_diff;
+
+  initial rd_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) begin
+    if (rd_have_reset) begin
+      if (rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (rd_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant, read domain.
+          rd_gray_diff = rd_gray_ptr ^ rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((rd_gray_diff & (rd_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. rd_empty must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using wr_gray_sync as it stood one rd_clk cycle ago.
+          assert (rd_empty == (rd_gray_ptr == wr_gray_sync_prev));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "empty".
+          assert (rd_empty);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: empty is reached again after having been non-empty
+        // (i.e. data flowed through and was fully drained at least once).
+        cover (!rd_empty_prev && rd_empty);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- skip checks entirely, same reasoning
+      // as the write domain above.
+    end
+
+    rd_gray_ptr_prev  <= rd_gray_ptr;
+    wr_gray_sync_prev <= wr_gray_sync;
+    rd_empty_prev     <= rd_empty;
+    rd_rst_n_prev     <= rd_rst_n;
+    rd_have_reset     <= rd_have_reset | !rd_rst_n;
+  end
+
+endmodule
+
+bind async_fifo async_fifo_formal #(
+    .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+) u_formal (.*);

+// counter.sv
+// Minimal toy design to validate the Yosys + SymbiYosys + solver formal flow
+// before applying formal methods to the real async FIFO.
+
+module counter (
+    input  logic       clk,
+    input  logic        rst,
+    output logic [1:0]  count
+);
+
+  always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
+    if (rst)
+      count <= 2'd0;
+    else
+      count <= count + 2'd1;
+  end
+
+  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // NOTE: these are IMMEDIATE assertions (plain statements inside a
+  // clocked always block), not concurrent SVA (`assert property (@(...))`).
+  // Plain Yosys (read_verilog -sv, no slang/Verific frontend) only
+  // parses this simpler form. It's enough to validate the tool flow.
+  // When we move to the real FIFO's temporal properties, we'll switch
+  // to the slang frontend for full concurrent-SVA support.
+  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
+  always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
+    // Safety: a 2-bit register can never hold a value above 3. Trivially
+    // true by construction -- a passing proof here just confirms the
+    // tool flow (parse -> prove -> pass/fail) works end to end.
+    assert (count <= 2'd3);
+
+    // Cover: prove count == 3 is actually reachable, so the assertion
+    // above isn't vacuously true (e.g. because of a stuck reset).
+    cover (count == 2'd3);
+  end
+
+endmodule

+`timescale 1ns / 1ps
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 1: Dual-Port RAM
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_mem #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4              // Depth = 2**ADDR_WIDTH = 16
+)(
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,    // Gated externally: only HIGH when not full
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data
+);
+
+    // ---- Storage array ----
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] mem [0:(1<<ADDR_WIDTH)-1];
+
+    // Synchronous write
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+        if (wr_en)
+            mem[wr_addr] <= wr_data;
+    end
+
+    // Combinational (async) read
+    assign rd_data = mem[rd_addr];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 2: 2-Flop Synchronizer
+// ==========================================================================
+module sync_2ff #(
+    parameter WIDTH = 1
+)(
+    input  logic             clk,       // Destination clock
+    input  logic             rst_n,     // Destination reset (active-low)
+    input  logic [WIDTH-1:0] d_in,      // Input from source domain
+    output logic [WIDTH-1:0] q_out      // Synchronized output in dest domain
+);
+
+    // Two-stage pipeline
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] meta_ff;  // Stage 1 — may go metastable
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] sync_ff;  // Stage 2 — resolved, safe to use
+
+    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
+        if (!rst_n) begin
+            meta_ff <= '0;
+            sync_ff <= '0;
+        end else begin
+            meta_ff <= d_in;
+            sync_ff <= meta_ff;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign q_out = sync_ff;
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 3: Write Pointer & Full Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    wr_clk,
+    input  logic                    wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    wr_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   wr_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    wr_full
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits (extra MSB for wrap detection)
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_next;
+    logic                wr_full_next;
+
+    // Increment logic
+    assign wr_bin_next  = wr_bin + (wr_en & ~wr_full);
+    assign wr_gray_next = wr_bin_next ^ (wr_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign wr_full_next = (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0]);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk or negedge wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (!wr_rst_n) begin
+            wr_bin <= '0;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            wr_full <= 1'b0;
+        end else begin
+            wr_bin <= wr_bin_next;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= wr_gray_next;
+            wr_full <= wr_full_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign wr_addr = wr_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 4: Read Pointer & Empty Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    rd_clk,
+    input  logic                    rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    rd_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   rd_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    rd_empty
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_next;
+    logic                rd_empty_next;
+
+    assign rd_bin_next = rd_bin + (rd_en & ~rd_empty);
+    assign rd_gray_next = rd_bin_next ^ (rd_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign rd_empty_next = (rd_gray_next == wr_gray_sync);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge rd_clk or negedge rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (!rd_rst_n) begin
+            rd_bin <= '0;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            rd_empty <= 1'b1;
+        end else begin
+            rd_bin <= rd_bin_next;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= rd_gray_next;
+            rd_empty <= rd_empty_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign rd_addr = rd_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Top-Level Module: Asynchronous FIFO
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    // Write domain
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    output logic                  wr_full,
+    // Read domain
+    input  logic                  rd_clk,
+    input  logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  rd_en,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data,
+    output logic                  rd_empty
+);
+
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync;
+
+    logic wr_en_gated;
+
+    assign wr_en_gated = wr_en & ~wr_full;
+
+    // RAM
+    async_fifo_mem #(
+        .DATA_WIDTH(DATA_WIDTH),
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_mem (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_en(wr_en_gated),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_data(wr_data),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_data(rd_data)
+    );
+
+    // Write pointer & full logic
+    async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_wr_ptr (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .wr_en(wr_en),
+        .rd_gray_sync(rd_gray_sync),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_gray_ptr(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .wr_full(wr_full)
+    );
+
+    // Read pointer & empty logic
+    async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_rd_ptr (
+        .rd_clk(rd_clk),
+        .rd_rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .rd_en(rd_en),
+        .wr_gray_sync(wr_gray_sync),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_gray_ptr(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .rd_empty(rd_empty)
+    );
+
+    // Synchronizers
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_wr2rd (
+        .clk(rd_clk),
+        .rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .d_in(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(wr_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_rd2wr (
+        .clk(wr_clk),
+        .rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .d_in(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(rd_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+endmodule

+// ============================================================================
+// Project     : FIFO Portfolio – Part 2: Asynchronous FIFO (CDC)
+// File        : async_fifo_tb.sv
+// Author      : [Your Name]
+// Date        : 2026-09-04
+// Description : Self-checking testbench for parameterizable Asynchronous FIFO
+//
+// CDC Testing Strategy:
+//   - We use independent clock generators with incommensurate frequencies
+//     (100 MHz vs 37 MHz) to ensure edges slide past each other, testing
+//     metastability conditions and synchronizer performance.
+//   - A SystemVerilog queue [$] acts as the reference model to verify data
+//     integrity and ordering across the clock domain crossing.
+// ============================================================================
+
+`timescale 1ns / 1ps
+
+module async_fifo_tb;
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // Parameters & Signals
+    // ============================================================
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8;
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4;
+    parameter FIFO_DEPTH = 1 << ADDR_WIDTH;
+
+    // Write Domain
+    logic                  wr_clk;
+    logic                  wr_rst_n;
+    logic                  wr_en;
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data;
+    logic                  wr_full;
+
+    // Read Domain
+    logic                  rd_clk;
+    logic                  rd_rst_n;
+    logic                  rd_en;
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data;
+    logic                  rd_empty;
+
+    // Reference model variables
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] ref_queue[$];
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] expected_data;
+
+    // Tracking variables
+    int errors = 0;
+    int writes_done = 0;
+    int reads_done = 0;
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // Clock Generation
+    // ============================================================
+    // WHY THESE FREQUENCIES?
+    // We want unaligned clock edges to thoroughly test the CDC logic.
+    // 100 MHz (10ns) and ~37.03 MHz (27ns) are effectively incommensurate.
+
+    // Write Clock: 100 MHz (10ns period) -> Fast writer
+    initial begin
+        wr_clk = 0;
+        forever #5 wr_clk = ~wr_clk;
+    end
+
+    // Read Clock: 37 MHz (27ns period) -> Slow reader
+    initial begin
+        rd_clk = 0;
+        forever #13.5 rd_clk = ~rd_clk;
+    end
+
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // DUT Instantiation
+    // ============================================================
+    async_fifo #(
+        .DATA_WIDTH (DATA_WIDTH),
+        .ADDR_WIDTH (ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) dut (
+        .wr_clk     (wr_clk),
+        .wr_rst_n   (wr_rst_n),
+        .wr_en      (wr_en),
+        .wr_data    (wr_data),
+        .wr_full    (wr_full),
+
+        .rd_clk     (rd_clk),
+        .rd_rst_n   (rd_rst_n),
+        .rd_en      (rd_en),
+        .rd_data    (rd_data),
+        .rd_empty   (rd_empty)
+    );
+
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // Tasks
+    // ============================================================
+
+    // Reset Task - Safely reset both domains
+    task reset_fifo();
+        $display("[TIME: %0t] Resetting FIFO...", $time);
+        wr_rst_n = 0;
+        rd_rst_n = 0;
+        wr_en    = 0;
+        rd_en    = 0;
+        wr_data  = 0;
+
+        // Hold reset for several slow clock cycles
+        #(27 * 3);
+
+        // De-assert reset (asynchronous domains so we split them, but staggered slightly)
+        @(negedge wr_clk); wr_rst_n = 1;
+        @(negedge rd_clk); rd_rst_n = 1;
+
+        // Wait for synchronizers to flush out any X's
+        #(27 * 3);
+        $display("[TIME: %0t] Reset complete.", $time);
+
+        // Clear reference queue
+        ref_queue.delete();
+        errors = 0;
+        writes_done = 0;
+        reads_done  = 0;
+    endtask
+
+    // Write Task - Asserts write if not full
+    task write_data(input logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] data);
+        @(negedge wr_clk);
+        if (wr_full) begin
+            $display("[TIME: %0t] WARNING: Attempted to write %h while FULL. Checking protection.", $time, data);
+            wr_en = 1;      // Drive en to test protection
+            wr_data = data;
+            @(negedge wr_clk);
+            wr_en = 0;
+        end else begin
+            wr_en = 1;
+            wr_data = data;
+            ref_queue.push_back(data);  // Update reference model
+            writes_done++;
+            @(negedge wr_clk);
+            wr_en = 0;
+        end
+    endtask
+
+    // Read Task - Pops data if not empty and verifies
+    task read_and_check();
+        @(negedge rd_clk);
+        if (rd_empty) begin
+            $display("[TIME: %0t] WARNING: Attempted to read while EMPTY. Checking protection.", $time);
+            rd_en = 1;     // Drive en to test protection
+            @(negedge rd_clk);
+            rd_en = 0;
+        end else begin
+            rd_en = 1;
+            @(negedge rd_clk); // Wait for combinational read data to settle on falling edge
+
+            if (ref_queue.size() == 0) begin
+                $display("[FAIL] [TIME: %0t] Read valid but reference queue is empty!", $time);
+                errors++;
+            end else begin
+                expected_data = ref_queue.pop_front();
+                if (rd_data !== expected_data) begin
+                    $display("[FAIL] [TIME: %0t] Data mismatch! Expected: %h, Got: %h", $time, expected_data, rd_data);
+                    errors++;
+                end else begin
+                    reads_done++;
+                    // $display("[PASS] [TIME: %0t] Let Rd_data = %h", $time, rd_data);
+                end
+            end
+
+            rd_en = 0;
+        end
+    endtask
+
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // Test Sequence
+    // ============================================================
+    initial begin
+        $display("\n============================================================");
+        $display("   ASYNC FIFO TESTBENCH STARTING");
+        $display("   Fast Writer (100MHz), Slow Reader (37MHz)");
+        $display("============================================================\n");
+
+        // --- Step 1: Initial Reset ---
+        reset_fifo();
+
+        // --- Step 2: Basic Read/Write ---
+        $display("\n--- Test 2: Basic Pipeline Read/Write ---");
+        write_data(8'hAA);
+        write_data(8'hBB);
+
+        // Wait for data to cross CDC into read domain (takes ~3 rd_clk cycles)
+        #(27 * 4);
+
+        read_and_check();
+        read_and_check();
+
+
+        // --- Step 3: Fast Write Burst (Testing Full Flag) ---
+        $display("\n--- Test 3: Fast Write Burst (Overflow check) ---");
+        // Our FIFO is depth 16. Let's write 20 items quickly.
+        // The read clock is slow, so it won't drain fast enough. Full should trigger.
+        for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) begin
+            write_data(8'h10 + i);
+        end
+
+        // We attempted 20 writes. 16 should succeed, 4 should drop.
+        // Wait for system to settle
+        #(27 * 4);
+
+        // Drain it completely
+        $display("Draining FIFO...");
+        while (ref_queue.size() > 0 || !rd_empty) begin
+            read_and_check();
+            if (rd_empty && ref_queue.size() > 0) begin
+                // Give it CDC time if empty is briefly true but we expect data
+                #(27 * 2);
+            end
+        end
+
+
+        // --- Step 4: Write during Empty / CDC Latency Test ---
+        $display("\n--- Test 4: Write checking CDC latency to Empty flag ---");
+        // Write 1 item. Read domain should NOT see it instantly due to 2FF sync.
+        write_data(8'hFF);
+
+        @(posedge rd_clk);
+        if (rd_empty) begin
+            $display("[TIME: %0t] Empty flag correctly remains asserted immediately after write (CDC latency).", $time);
+        end else begin
+            $display("[FAIL] Empty flag de-asserted too quickly. CDC might be bypassed!");
+            errors++;
+        end
+
+        // Wait for CDC propagation
+        #(27 * 4);
+        read_and_check();
+
+
+        // --- Step 5: Simultaneous Continuous Traffic ---
+        $display("\n--- Test 5: Continuous Mixed Traffic ---");
+        // Run concurrent write and read loops.
+        // Because clocks are separate, we use fork-join to run them in parallel.
+        fork
+            // Write Thread
+            begin
+                for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) begin
+                    // Write occasionally when not full
+                    @(negedge wr_clk);
+                    if (!wr_full && ($urandom_range(0, 100) > 20)) begin
+                        write_data($urandom_range(0, 255));
+                    end
+                end
+            end
+
+            // Read Thread
+            begin
+                for (int i = 0; i < 150; i++) begin
+                    // Read occasionally when not empty
+                    @(negedge rd_clk);
+                    if (!rd_empty && ($urandom_range(0, 100) > 30)) begin
+                        read_and_check();
+                    end
+                end
+            end
+        join
+
+        // Wait to settle, then drain whatever is left
+        #(27 * 5);
+        while (ref_queue.size() > 0) begin
+            read_and_check();
+        end
+
+
+        // ============================================================
+        // Test Summary
+        // ============================================================
+        $display("\n============================================================");
+        $display("   TEST SUMMARY");
+        $display("============================================================");
+        $display("   Writes completed : %0d", writes_done);
+        $display("   Reads completed  : %0d", reads_done);
+
+        if (errors == 0 && writes_done == reads_done && writes_done > 0) begin
+            $display("\n   RESULT:  PASSED  [All %0d items matched exactly]", writes_done);
+        end else begin
+            $display("\n   RESULT:  FAILED  [%0d errors found]", errors);
+            if (writes_done != reads_done)
+                $display("   WARNING: Mismatch in total read vs total written.");
+        end
+        $display("============================================================\n");
+
+        $finish;
+    end
+
+endmodule

+// async_fifo_formal.sv (v3)
+// Formal property set for the Gray-code CDC async FIFO, Phase 1.
+//
+// v1 used concurrent SVA (assert property / $past / $rose / $fell) --
+// unsupported by yosys-slang's current synthesis path.
+// v2 switched to immediate assertions, but relied on `initial assume
+// (!wr_rst_n)` to force a known-good starting state -- also unsupported
+// ("reading net state during design initialization unsupported"), since
+// an `initial` block can only set register values, not sample a live
+// input signal (there's no such thing as "the input's value before
+// time begins" in real hardware).
+//
+// v3 fixes this properly: a STICKY "have we ever actually observed a
+// real reset" flag per domain, set permanently to 1 the first time
+// rst_n is seen low at any clock edge. Checks are only enabled once
+// that flag is set. This is arguably the more correct technique anyway
+// -- it doesn't force reset to happen at exactly time 0, only requires
+// it to have happened at some point in the design's history before we
+// start trusting internal-register consistency, which is the actual
+// real-world guarantee.
+//
+// Properties covered:
+//   1. Gray-code one-bit-change invariant (wr and rd domains)
+//   2. Reset behavior: wr_full low / rd_empty high on the first cycle
+//      after each domain's reset releases
+//   3. wr_full / rd_empty exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+//      using the manually-tracked previous-cycle synchronized pointer
+//   4. Cover: prove full is reachable, prove recovery from full, prove
+//      empty is reached again after data has flowed through
+
+module async_fifo_formal #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+) (
+    // Write domain
+    input logic                  wr_clk,
+    input logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input logic                  wr_en,
+    input logic                  wr_full,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync,
+    // Read domain
+    input logic                  rd_clk,
+    input logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input logic                  rd_en,
+    input logic                  rd_empty,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr,
+    input logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync
+);
+
+  // ================== Write-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                wr_full_prev;
+  logic                wr_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                wr_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_diff;
+
+  initial wr_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+    // Only trust history once a real reset has actually been observed
+    // at some point -- otherwise the solver is free to start wr_bin
+    // and wr_gray_ptr at two unrelated arbitrary values, which breaks
+    // any comparison for reasons that have nothing to do with the RTL.
+    if (wr_have_reset) begin
+      if (wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (wr_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant -- the property that makes
+          // crossing this pointer through a 2-flop synchronizer safe.
+          // (diff & (diff-1)) == 0 is true iff diff is zero or a single
+          // bit -- the same semantics as $onehot0, without relying on
+          // that system task (unsupported by the current frontend).
+          wr_gray_diff = wr_gray_ptr ^ wr_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((wr_gray_diff & (wr_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. wr_full must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using rd_gray_sync as it stood one wr_clk cycle ago (that's
+          // the value actually captured into wr_full_next on that edge).
+          assert (wr_full == (
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+            (wr_gray_ptr[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync_prev[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0])
+          ));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "not full".
+          assert (!wr_full);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: full is reachable, and recovery from full is reachable.
+        cover (wr_full);
+        cover (wr_full_prev && !wr_full);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- async reset can snap pointers to 0
+      // between any two samples, so no invariant is expected to hold
+      // this cycle. Skip checks entirely until reset is released again.
+    end
+
+    wr_gray_ptr_prev  <= wr_gray_ptr;
+    rd_gray_sync_prev <= rd_gray_sync;
+    wr_full_prev      <= wr_full;
+    wr_rst_n_prev     <= wr_rst_n;
+    wr_have_reset     <= wr_have_reset | !wr_rst_n;
+  end
+
+  // ================== Read-domain checker ==================
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_sync_prev;
+  logic                rd_empty_prev;
+  logic                rd_rst_n_prev;
+  logic                rd_have_reset;
+  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_diff;
+
+  initial rd_have_reset = 1'b0;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge rd_clk) begin
+    if (rd_have_reset) begin
+      if (rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (rd_rst_n_prev) begin
+          // Both this cycle and the previous one are out of reset --
+          // safe to compare against tracked history.
+
+          // 1. Gray one-bit-change invariant, read domain.
+          rd_gray_diff = rd_gray_ptr ^ rd_gray_ptr_prev;
+          assert ((rd_gray_diff & (rd_gray_diff - 1'b1)) == '0);
+
+          // 3. rd_empty must exactly match the Gray-comparison formula,
+          // using wr_gray_sync as it stood one rd_clk cycle ago.
+          assert (rd_empty == (rd_gray_ptr == wr_gray_sync_prev));
+        end else begin
+          // 2. First active cycle after reset release: must start "empty".
+          assert (rd_empty);
+        end
+
+        // 4. Cover: empty is reached again after having been non-empty
+        // (i.e. data flowed through and was fully drained at least once).
+        cover (!rd_empty_prev && rd_empty);
+      end
+      // else: currently in reset -- skip checks entirely, same reasoning
+      // as the write domain above.
+    end
+
+    rd_gray_ptr_prev  <= rd_gray_ptr;
+    wr_gray_sync_prev <= wr_gray_sync;
+    rd_empty_prev     <= rd_empty;
+    rd_rst_n_prev     <= rd_rst_n;
+    rd_have_reset     <= rd_have_reset | !rd_rst_n;
+  end
+
+endmodule
+
+bind async_fifo async_fifo_formal #(
+    .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+) u_formal (.*);

+// counter.sv
+// Minimal toy design to validate the Yosys + SymbiYosys + solver formal flow
+// before applying formal methods to the real async FIFO.
+
+module counter (
+    input  logic       clk,
+    input  logic        rst,
+    output logic [1:0]  count
+);
+
+  always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
+    if (rst)
+      count <= 2'd0;
+    else
+      count <= count + 2'd1;
+  end
+
+  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // NOTE: these are IMMEDIATE assertions (plain statements inside a
+  // clocked always block), not concurrent SVA (`assert property (@(...))`).
+  // Plain Yosys (read_verilog -sv, no slang/Verific frontend) only
+  // parses this simpler form. It's enough to validate the tool flow.
+  // When we move to the real FIFO's temporal properties, we'll switch
+  // to the slang frontend for full concurrent-SVA support.
+  // --------------------------------------------------------------------
+  always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
+    // Safety: a 2-bit register can never hold a value above 3. Trivially
+    // true by construction -- a passing proof here just confirms the
+    // tool flow (parse -> prove -> pass/fail) works end to end.
+    assert (count <= 2'd3);
+
+    // Cover: prove count == 3 is actually reachable, so the assertion
+    // above isn't vacuously true (e.g. because of a stuck reset).
+    cover (count == 2'd3);
+  end
+
+endmodule

+`timescale 1ns / 1ps
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 1: Dual-Port RAM
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_mem #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4              // Depth = 2**ADDR_WIDTH = 16
+)(
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,    // Gated externally: only HIGH when not full
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data
+);
+
+    // ---- Storage array ----
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] mem [0:(1<<ADDR_WIDTH)-1];
+
+    // Synchronous write
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk) begin
+        if (wr_en)
+            mem[wr_addr] <= wr_data;
+    end
+
+    // Combinational (async) read
+    assign rd_data = mem[rd_addr];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 2: 2-Flop Synchronizer
+// ==========================================================================
+module sync_2ff #(
+    parameter WIDTH = 1
+)(
+    input  logic             clk,       // Destination clock
+    input  logic             rst_n,     // Destination reset (active-low)
+    input  logic [WIDTH-1:0] d_in,      // Input from source domain
+    output logic [WIDTH-1:0] q_out      // Synchronized output in dest domain
+);
+
+    // Two-stage pipeline
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] meta_ff;  // Stage 1 — may go metastable
+    logic [WIDTH-1:0] sync_ff;  // Stage 2 — resolved, safe to use
+
+    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
+        if (!rst_n) begin
+            meta_ff <= '0;
+            sync_ff <= '0;
+        end else begin
+            meta_ff <= d_in;
+            sync_ff <= meta_ff;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign q_out = sync_ff;
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 3: Write Pointer & Full Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    wr_clk,
+    input  logic                    wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    wr_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   wr_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    wr_full
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits (extra MSB for wrap detection)
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wr_gray_next;
+    logic                wr_full_next;
+
+    // Increment logic
+    assign wr_bin_next  = wr_bin + (wr_en & ~wr_full);
+    assign wr_gray_next = wr_bin_next ^ (wr_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign wr_full_next = (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH]     != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH])   &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-1]   != rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-1]) &&
+                          (wr_gray_next[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0] == rd_gray_sync[ADDR_WIDTH-2:0]);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge wr_clk or negedge wr_rst_n) begin
+        if (!wr_rst_n) begin
+            wr_bin <= '0;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            wr_full <= 1'b0;
+        end else begin
+            wr_bin <= wr_bin_next;
+            wr_gray_ptr <= wr_gray_next;
+            wr_full <= wr_full_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign wr_addr = wr_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Module 4: Read Pointer & Empty Flag Generation
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    input  logic                    rd_clk,
+    input  logic                    rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                    rd_en,
+    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     wr_gray_sync,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   rd_addr,
+    output logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]     rd_gray_ptr,
+    output logic                    rd_empty
+);
+
+    // Binary pointer: ADDR_WIDTH+1 bits
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_bin_next;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rd_gray_next;
+    logic                rd_empty_next;
+
+    assign rd_bin_next = rd_bin + (rd_en & ~rd_empty);
+    assign rd_gray_next = rd_bin_next ^ (rd_bin_next >> 1);
+    assign rd_empty_next = (rd_gray_next == wr_gray_sync);
+
+    always_ff @(posedge rd_clk or negedge rd_rst_n) begin
+        if (!rd_rst_n) begin
+            rd_bin <= '0;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= '0;
+            rd_empty <= 1'b1;
+        end else begin
+            rd_bin <= rd_bin_next;
+            rd_gray_ptr <= rd_gray_next;
+            rd_empty <= rd_empty_next;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign rd_addr = rd_bin[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0];
+
+endmodule
+
+
+// ==========================================================================
+// Top-Level Module: Asynchronous FIFO
+// ==========================================================================
+module async_fifo #(
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4
+)(
+    // Write domain
+    input  logic                  wr_clk,
+    input  logic                  wr_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  wr_en,
+    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data,
+    output logic                  wr_full,
+    // Read domain
+    input  logic                  rd_clk,
+    input  logic                  rd_rst_n,
+    input  logic                  rd_en,
+    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data,
+    output logic                  rd_empty
+);
+
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] wr_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] rd_addr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_ptr;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   wr_gray_sync;
+    logic [ADDR_WIDTH:0]   rd_gray_sync;
+
+    logic wr_en_gated;
+
+    assign wr_en_gated = wr_en & ~wr_full;
+
+    // RAM
+    async_fifo_mem #(
+        .DATA_WIDTH(DATA_WIDTH),
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_mem (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_en(wr_en_gated),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_data(wr_data),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_data(rd_data)
+    );
+
+    // Write pointer & full logic
+    async_fifo_wr_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_wr_ptr (
+        .wr_clk(wr_clk),
+        .wr_rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .wr_en(wr_en),
+        .rd_gray_sync(rd_gray_sync),
+        .wr_addr(wr_addr),
+        .wr_gray_ptr(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .wr_full(wr_full)
+    );
+
+    // Read pointer & empty logic
+    async_fifo_rd_ptr #(
+        .ADDR_WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) u_rd_ptr (
+        .rd_clk(rd_clk),
+        .rd_rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .rd_en(rd_en),
+        .wr_gray_sync(wr_gray_sync),
+        .rd_addr(rd_addr),
+        .rd_gray_ptr(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .rd_empty(rd_empty)
+    );
+
+    // Synchronizers
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_wr2rd (
+        .clk(rd_clk),
+        .rst_n(rd_rst_n),
+        .d_in(wr_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(wr_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+    sync_2ff #(
+        .WIDTH(ADDR_WIDTH + 1)
+    ) u_sync_rd2wr (
+        .clk(wr_clk),
+        .rst_n(wr_rst_n),
+        .d_in(rd_gray_ptr),
+        .q_out(rd_gray_sync)
+    );
+
+endmodule

+// ============================================================================
+// Project     : FIFO Portfolio – Part 2: Asynchronous FIFO (CDC)
+// File        : async_fifo_tb.sv
+// Author      : [Your Name]
+// Date        : 2026-09-04
+// Description : Self-checking testbench for parameterizable Asynchronous FIFO
+//
+// CDC Testing Strategy:
+//   - We use independent clock generators with incommensurate frequencies
+//     (100 MHz vs 37 MHz) to ensure edges slide past each other, testing
+//     metastability conditions and synchronizer performance.
+//   - A SystemVerilog queue [$] acts as the reference model to verify data
+//     integrity and ordering across the clock domain crossing.
+// ============================================================================
+
+`timescale 1ns / 1ps
+
+module async_fifo_tb;
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // Parameters & Signals
+    // ============================================================
+    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8;
+    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 4;
+    parameter FIFO_DEPTH = 1 << ADDR_WIDTH;
+
+    // Write Domain
+    logic                  wr_clk;
+    logic                  wr_rst_n;
+    logic                  wr_en;
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wr_data;
+    logic                  wr_full;
+
+    // Read Domain
+    logic                  rd_clk;
+    logic                  rd_rst_n;
+    logic                  rd_en;
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] rd_data;
+    logic                  rd_empty;
+
+    // Reference model variables
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] ref_queue[$];
+    logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] expected_data;
+
+    // Tracking variables
+    int errors = 0;
+    int writes_done = 0;
+    int reads_done = 0;
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // Clock Generation
+    // ============================================================
+    // WHY THESE FREQUENCIES?
+    // We want unaligned clock edges to thoroughly test the CDC logic.
+    // 100 MHz (10ns) and ~37.03 MHz (27ns) are effectively incommensurate.
+
+    // Write Clock: 100 MHz (10ns period) -> Fast writer
+    initial begin
+        wr_clk = 0;
+        forever #5 wr_clk = ~wr_clk;
+    end
+
+    // Read Clock: 37 MHz (27ns period) -> Slow reader
+    initial begin
+        rd_clk = 0;
+        forever #13.5 rd_clk = ~rd_clk;
+    end
+
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // DUT Instantiation
+    // ============================================================
+    async_fifo #(
+        .DATA_WIDTH (DATA_WIDTH),
+        .ADDR_WIDTH (ADDR_WIDTH)
+    ) dut (
+        .wr_clk     (wr_clk),
+        .wr_rst_n   (wr_rst_n),
+        .wr_en      (wr_en),
+        .wr_data    (wr_data),
+        .wr_full    (wr_full),
+
+        .rd_clk     (rd_clk),
+        .rd_rst_n   (rd_rst_n),
+        .rd_en      (rd_en),
+        .rd_data    (rd_data),
+        .rd_empty   (rd_empty)
+    );
+
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // Tasks
+    // ============================================================
+
+    // Reset Task - Safely reset both domains
+    task reset_fifo();
+        $display("[TIME: %0t] Resetting FIFO...", $time);
+        wr_rst_n = 0;
+        rd_rst_n = 0;
+        wr_en    = 0;
+        rd_en    = 0;
+        wr_data  = 0;
+
+        // Hold reset for several slow clock cycles
+        #(27 * 3);
+
+        // De-assert reset (asynchronous domains so we split them, but staggered slightly)
+        @(negedge wr_clk); wr_rst_n = 1;
+        @(negedge rd_clk); rd_rst_n = 1;
+
+        // Wait for synchronizers to flush out any X's
+        #(27 * 3);
+        $display("[TIME: %0t] Reset complete.", $time);
+
+        // Clear reference queue
+        ref_queue.delete();
+        errors = 0;
+        writes_done = 0;
+        reads_done  = 0;
+    endtask
+
+    // Write Task - Asserts write if not full
+    task write_data(input logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] data);
+        @(negedge wr_clk);
+        if (wr_full) begin
+            $display("[TIME: %0t] WARNING: Attempted to write %h while FULL. Checking protection.", $time, data);
+            wr_en = 1;      // Drive en to test protection
+            wr_data = data;
+            @(negedge wr_clk);
+            wr_en = 0;
+        end else begin
+            wr_en = 1;
+            wr_data = data;
+            ref_queue.push_back(data);  // Update reference model
+            writes_done++;
+            @(negedge wr_clk);
+            wr_en = 0;
+        end
+    endtask
+
+    // Read Task - Pops data if not empty and verifies
+    task read_and_check();
+        @(negedge rd_clk);
+        if (rd_empty) begin
+            $display("[TIME: %0t] WARNING: Attempted to read while EMPTY. Checking protection.", $time);
+            rd_en = 1;     // Drive en to test protection
+            @(negedge rd_clk);
+            rd_en = 0;
+        end else begin
+            rd_en = 1;
+            @(negedge rd_clk); // Wait for combinational read data to settle on falling edge
+
+            if (ref_queue.size() == 0) begin
+                $display("[FAIL] [TIME: %0t] Read valid but reference queue is empty!", $time);
+                errors++;
+            end else begin
+                expected_data = ref_queue.pop_front();
+                if (rd_data !== expected_data) begin
+                    $display("[FAIL] [TIME: %0t] Data mismatch! Expected: %h, Got: %h", $time, expected_data, rd_data);
+                    errors++;
+                end else begin
+                    reads_done++;
+                    // $display("[PASS] [TIME: %0t] Let Rd_data = %h", $time, rd_data);
+                end
+            end
+
+            rd_en = 0;
+        end
+    endtask
+
+
+    // ============================================================
+    // Test Sequence
+    // ============================================================
+    initial begin
+        $display("\n============================================================");
+        $display("   ASYNC FIFO TESTBENCH STARTING");
+        $display("   Fast Writer (100MHz), Slow Reader (37MHz)");
+        $display("============================================================\n");
+
+        // --- Step 1: Initial Reset ---
+        reset_fifo();
+
+        // --- Step 2: Basic Read/Write ---
+        $display("\n--- Test 2: Basic Pipeline Read/Write ---");
+        write_data(8'hAA);
+        write_data(8'hBB);
+
+        // Wait for data to cross CDC into read domain (takes ~3 rd_clk cycles)
+        #(27 * 4);
+
+        read_and_check();
+        read_and_check();
+
+
+        // --- Step 3: Fast Write Burst (Testing Full Flag) ---
+        $display("\n--- Test 3: Fast Write Burst (Overflow check) ---");
+        // Our FIFO is depth 16. Let's write 20 items quickly.
+        // The read clock is slow, so it won't drain fast enough. Full should trigger.
+        for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) begin
+            write_data(8'h10 + i);
+        end
+
+        // We attempted 20 writes. 16 should succeed, 4 should drop.
+        // Wait for system to settle
+        #(27 * 4);
+
+        // Drain it completely
+        $display("Draining FIFO...");
+        while (ref_queue.size() > 0 || !rd_empty) begin
+            read_and_check();
+            if (rd_empty && ref_queue.size() > 0) begin
+                // Give it CDC time if empty is briefly true but we expect data
+                #(27 * 2);
+            end
+        end
+
+
+        // --- Step 4: Write during Empty / CDC Latency Test ---
+        $display("\n--- Test 4: Write checking CDC latency to Empty flag ---");
+        // Write 1 item. Read domain should NOT see it instantly due to 2FF sync.
+        write_data(8'hFF);
+
+        @(posedge rd_clk);
+        if (rd_empty) begin
+            $display("[TIME: %0t] Empty flag correctly remains asserted immediately after write (CDC latency).", $time);
+        end else begin
+            $display("[FAIL] Empty flag de-asserted too quickly. CDC might be bypassed!");
+            errors++;
+        end
+
+        // Wait for CDC propagation
+        #(27 * 4);
+        read_and_check();
+
+
+        // --- Step 5: Simultaneous Continuous Traffic ---
+        $display("\n--- Test 5: Continuous Mixed Traffic ---");
+        // Run concurrent write and read loops.
+        // Because clocks are separate, we use fork-join to run them in parallel.
+        fork
+            // Write Thread
+            begin
+                for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) begin
+                    // Write occasionally when not full
+                    @(negedge wr_clk);
+                    if (!wr_full && ($urandom_range(0, 100) > 20)) begin
+                        write_data($urandom_range(0, 255));
+                    end
+                end
+            end
+
+            // Read Thread
+            begin
+                for (int i = 0; i < 150; i++) begin
+                    // Read occasionally when not empty
+                    @(negedge rd_clk);
+                    if (!rd_empty && ($urandom_range(0, 100) > 30)) begin
+                        read_and_check();
+                    end
+                end
+            end
+        join
+
+        // Wait to settle, then drain whatever is left
+        #(27 * 5);
+        while (ref_queue.size() > 0) begin
+            read_and_check();
+        end
+
+
+        // ============================================================
+        // Test Summary
+        // ============================================================
+        $display("\n============================================================");
+        $display("   TEST SUMMARY");
+        $display("============================================================");
+        $display("   Writes completed : %0d", writes_done);
+        $display("   Reads completed  : %0d", reads_done);
+
+        if (errors == 0 && writes_done == reads_done && writes_done > 0) begin
+            $display("\n   RESULT:  PASSED  [All %0d items matched exactly]", writes_done);
+        end else begin
+            $display("\n   RESULT:  FAILED  [%0d errors found]", errors);
+            if (writes_done != reads_done)
+                $display("   WARNING: Mismatch in total read vs total written.");
+        end
+        $display("============================================================\n");
+
+        $finish;
+    end
+
+endmodule
